text:
Nic Dowd made his name as Washington's shutdown center over 506 games, and Vegas brought him in last season for that same role. At 36, the Huntsville, Alabama native (one of only three NHL players from the state) is still killing minutes, but the numbers are stark. He has no goals and three assists in 20 games, with just six shots on goal.

At five on five his line is getting buried: 35.1% of expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his team's share drops by almost 22 points relative to when he sits. Some of the scoring drought is luck. Vegas has scored 4.5 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there, and that tends to swing back.

But the process isn't flattering either. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level in 2025-26 (-1.1 wins), with his team creating little with him on. His minutes have dipped to 10.9 over his last ten as Vegas has rolled off four straight wins, so the question is how big his role stays if the Golden Knights keep winning without him driving it.
headline: Dowd is still searching for a goal in Vegas
